experimental_procedure: Scheme 1. General Synthetic Approach to Pyrrolonesa A. General procedure for the microwave-accelerated synthesis of 2,5-dimethyl-1-aryl-1H-pyrroles(6). 2,5-Hexandione (4) (1 mmol), the appropriate aniline 5a-x (1.2 equiv) and p-toluenesulfonic acid bound with silica gel (0.4 equiv) were mixed in an oven dried pressure vial with a magnetic stirrer bar. The vessel was placed in a microwave oven and heated (180 °C, 15-20 min) under microwave irradiation (0-400 W at 2.45 GHz). After stirring for a further 15 min at room temperature the reaction mixture was filtered and the residual silica washed with DCM (10 mL). The solvent was removed under reduced pressure to give the corresponding 2,5-dimethyl-1-aryl-1H-pyrrole 6a-x (80-90% yield, purity >95% by LCMS). B. General Procedure for the synthesis of formyl pyrroles (7a-r). Phosphorous oxychloride (0.5 mL, 6 mmol) was added dropwise to stirred ice-cooled DMF (12 mL) under a N2 atmosphere. The mixture was then allowed to warm to room temperature over 15 min, a solution of the pyrrole (6a-r) (1 mmol) in DMF (5 mL) added and the mixture heated at 100 °C for 3 h under a N2 atmosphere. After cooling, 30% aq NaOH was added dropwise to pH 10.0 and the resulting precipitate was filtered, washed several times with water and dried in vacuo to give the corresponding formyl derivative 7a-r (80-95%), which was generally used without further purification.
